item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q018_tal_effector_repeat_lengths","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, all three are homologous members of the TAL (transcription activator-like) effector family a.298.1.1 (sunid 267609), despite their very different SEQRES lengths: d2kq5a_ is a 51-residue PthA fragment from Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. citri, d3v6pa_ is a 373-residue dHax3 repeat array from Xanthomonas, and d4cj9a_ is a 752-residue BurrH array from Burkholderia rhizoxinica. TAL-effector domains are modular tandem-repeat proteins, so expansion or contraction of a conserved alpha-helical repeat unit changes total length without changing the family-defining repeat architecture. Their shared classification is specifically family a.298.1.1 within TAL effector-like superfamily a.298.1, left-handed alpha-alpha superhelix fold a.298, and all-alpha class a; similarity only at the broader superfamily, fold, or class level would imply progressively weaker evolutionary relatedness than the shared family assignment. The family label supports homology of the repeat-domain architecture, but it does not establish identical full-length functions, orthology, DNA targets, or host targets. In particular, target specificity depends strongly on repeat-variable residues, so transferring dHax3 or PthA binding specificity to BurrH from the SCOPe assignment alone would be unsafe; that requires repeat-residue/target-sequence analysis and preferably direct DNA-binding and functional evidence. Likewise, a short repeat fragment such as d2kq5a_ can guide modeling of a local repeat but is not by itself a complete template for the curvature, repeat register, termini, or packing of the much longer arrays. Representative selection should therefore match repeat number, sequence/RVD composition, and the intended structural or functional question rather than treating the shortest or longest entry as universally representative.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge","/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d2kq5a_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d3v6pa_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d4cj9a_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/264989","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/265556","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/265996","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267704","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267705","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267706","/api/v1/sequences/sids/d2kq5a_?release=2.08","/api/v1/sequences/sids/d3v6pa_?release=2.08","/api/v1/sequences/sids/d4cj9a_?release=2.08","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267645","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267646","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267647","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267609","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267596","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267589","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/46456"]}]}
